   • r23:1187-1260 LEADING CANONICAL `DAYS BETWEEN TWO DATES` block. Keyword anchors at r23:1189: `days between two dates, days since signup, time to first purchase in days, ... days between event A and event B, lag in days, gap in days.`
   • r23:1245 decision table row: `Days from signup to first purchase | signup_date | MIN(order_date) | date_diff('day', signup_date, MIN(order_date))` — same shape as the event-A-vs-event-B self-join (signup is an event_type, first-purchase is another event_type; same entity = customer).
   • r23:1249 row: `Days between two events of the same kind | lag_event_at | event_at | date_diff('day', lag_event_at, event_at) (pair with LAG(event_at) OVER (...))` — covers the within-entity event-sequence case.
   • r23:1191 THE ONE FACT: `Trino has NO date − date integer-subtraction operator.` The date_diff('day', earlier, later) is mandatory; arg order matters (third arg = later → positive result).
   • Self-join shape SYNTHESIZABLE-FROM-PRIMITIVES: `SELECT e1.entity_id, date_diff('day', e1.ts, e2.ts) AS days_between FROM events e1 JOIN events e2 ON e1.entity_id = e2.entity_id WHERE e1.event_type = 'A' AND e2.event_type = 'B'` — composes the date_diff primitive (r23:1191+) with a self-join (covered at r07:1719+ for self-join in YoY context, and r23 §3.1G for top-1-per-group self-join patterns).

Both shapes findable.
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified at trino.io/docs/current/functions/datetime.html): `date_diff(unit, timestamp1, timestamp2) -> bigint — Returns timestamp2 - timestamp1 expressed in terms of unit.` Match verified at r23:1191. No edits needed.

3) GENERATE A DATE SERIES / CALENDAR SPINE TO FILL GAPS (sequence(date1, date2, INTERVAL '1' DAY) → array → CROSS JOIN UNNEST → LEFT JOIN data, COALESCE zero-fill) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r07:862 LEADING CANONICAL signature pin: `sequence(start, stop) -> array (integer or date — step defaults to +1 if start <= stop, else -1); sequence(start, stop, step) -> array (integer step for ints; INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND or INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH step for dates and timestamps). Both bounds are INCLUSIVE. There is NO generate_series function in Trino — generate_series is the Postgres name; on Trino you write sequence(...) and UNNEST it to rows.` Keyword anchors: `Trino generate_series, Trino date spine, Trino generate range of dates, Trino row spine, Trino generate calendar, Trino sequence function signature, Trino integer range, Trino date range UNNEST.`
   • r07:848 short example: `FROM UNNEST(sequence(0, 29)) AS t(n)` — basic integer spine.
   • r07:1028 LEFT-JOIN-with-COALESCE-zero-fill: `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(sequence(lo, hi, INTERVAL '1' DAY)) AS t(d)` in a calendar CTE, then LEFT JOIN facts to spine + COALESCE(metric, 0).
   • r07:1049 explicit literal-bounds form: `SELECT d AS day FROM UNNEST(sequence(DATE '2026-05-01', DATE '2026-05-31', INTERVAL '1' DAY)) AS t(d)`.
   • r07:974 docs-correct usage rule: `Build the dense grid. CROSS JOIN UNNEST(sequence(min_ts, max_ts, INTERVAL '1' MINUTE)) × distinct entities (devices / users / tenants / products). The grid CTE contains every (entity, ts) pair you want in the output, with NO measure column yet. DO NOT build the spine from SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('day', event_ts) FROM facts — days with zero events across ALL entities will be MISSING.`
   • r07:999 the GROUP-BY-with-aggregate-in-spine parse-error inoculation (iter573 PIN): two correct forms (scalar-subquery the MIN/MAX bound OR bounds CTE + sequence over interval).
   • r07:1141 dynamic-bound form: `sequence(...)` inside a parameterized window.
   • r07:1456 cross-link: `Resource 07 § sequence() (the canonical date-spine generator — pair date_add with sequence when generating per-row offsets in calendar-spine joins).`
   • r23:2190 dialect-portability table: `GENERATE_SERIES(...) as a table function | PostgreSQL | NOT supported by that name. Use Trino's sequence(start, stop, step) returning an array, then UNNEST.` With Trino-rewrite recipe: `SELECT n FROM UNNEST(sequence(1, 10)) AS t(n);`
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified at trino.io/docs/current/functions/array.html on 2026-06-08 via WebFetch): `sequence(start, stop) — increments by 1 if start ≤ stop, otherwise -1. sequence(start, stop, step) — step can be INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND or INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH for dates/timestamps. Returns array. INCLUSIVE on both ends.` Matches r07:862 verbatim. No edits needed.
